## PARKER-HANNIFIN CORPORATION (NYSE: PH)

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
■ RS2 v2.0 INTEGRATED INVESTMENT ANALYSIS
■ Ticker: PH | Specialty Industrial Machinery | T0 = 2026-09-10
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SECTION 0. ANALYSIS OVERVIEW (ENTERPRISE CLASSIFICATION & MODEL SELECTION)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

0-1. ARCHETYPE DETERMINATION
Selected: **B. QUALITY COMPOUNDER** (primary), with acknowledged
Cyclical (C) sub-character in the Diversified Industrial half.

Three+ supporting reasons:
 R1. Sustained margin ascent on a ~flat asset base: operating margin
     16.4% (12-yr median) → 23.6% (FY26) [Actual: SEC pack §7].
     This is structural, not a cyclical spike alone.
 R2. Return of capital discipline: 70 consecutive fiscal years of
     increasing annual dividends per share; dividend raised 11% in
     FY26 [Actual: PH press release 2026-08-06]. Net share issuance
     -1.6% (1yr), -1.1% (3yr CAGR) [Actual: §7].
 R3. Earnings quality: accruals ratio -0.0237 (negative = cash-backed
     earnings); Piotroski 7/8 on evaluable items [Actual: §7].
 R4. Increasingly aftermarket/annuity-weighted profit mix via
     Aerospace Systems. This is the single most important archetype
     fact: it converts what would be a pure-Cyclical model into a
     Quality Compounder with a durable installed-base revenue layer.

0-2. VALUATION ENGINE SELECTED
**ENGINE 1 — Traditional DCF + Multiples.**
Rationale: positive, growing FCF; identifiable capital structure;
an addressable discount-rate derivation; no binary regulatory event;
no option-led future cash flow dependence (core revenue > 95% of EV).
Engine 4 (Expectation-Driven) is NOT appropriate: PH has no
meaningful revenue from unproven optionality.
Engine 5 is categorically inapplicable.

0-3. ARCHETYPE TRANSITION CHECK
PH is NOT in archetype transition. It completed the
Cyclical → Quality transition roughly FY2021-FY2023 (Meggitt
integration; aerospace mix shift). Evidence: operating margin
stability improved, revenue is 1.7x its FY2015 level with
operating margin +7.2pp [Estimate: 16.4% → 23.6%].

NOTE ON CYCLICAL RESIDUAL — I do NOT apply a blended Engine 2
weight. Reason: the cyclical component (Diversified Industrial,
~$15.4B of revenue at Q4 FY26 run-rate) is being explicitly
guided into a "broadening recovery", meaning the cycle position
is EARLY, not late. Applying trough-normalization to a business
at the start of a recovery would understate value. I instead
carry cyclicality inside the Bear scenario (SECTION 4).

0-4. WHY NOT AN ALTERNATIVE ENGINE
 If Engine 2 (Cycle-Adjusted) had been used: mid-cycle normaliz-
 ation applied to FY26's 23.6% margin (vs 16.4% 12-yr median)
 would have produced a materially lower value and ignored the
 explicit FY31 30%-segment-margin target. That target is a
 company commitment, not a trend extrapolation, and Engine 2
 cannot price it.
 If Engine 4 had been used: the Filtration/CIRCOR acquisitions
 would be misclassified as "optionality" rather than as
 contracted, closed, cash-generating businesses. Error.

DATA INTEGRITY FINDING (declared up front)
 The data pack's FY2026 annual column is VERIFIED against the
 primary source. Pack §5 FY2026: revenue $21.499B, net income
 $3.649B, OCF $4.364B, capex $0.459B, FCF $3.905B.
 PH press release 2026-08-06: "Sales increased 8.3% to a record
 $21.5 billion... Cash flow from operations was a record $4.4
 billion... free cash flow $3.9 billion."
 → Five-for-five agreement. The pack's FY26 annual row is
   treated as [Actual] and is trustworthy.
 SECURITY OF THE TTM WINDOW — DECLARED DEFECT
 Pack §3 TTM is withheld as "stranded" (fiscal anchor 2025-06-30).
 Pack §4 ends 2026-03-31 (fiscal Q3). The PRICE DATE is
 2026-09-10. FY26 ended 2026-06-30 (Q4 revenue $5,755M, net
 income $1,091M — retrieved from the press release, absent from
 the pack). Therefore the pack is ONE QUARTER AND ONE MATERIAL
 TRANSACTION BEHIND the price. I have patched both. Any analysis
 that used the pack alone would have valued a pre-Filtration
 Parker against a post-Filtration market price. That is the
 largest single error available in this dataset, and it is why
 I retrieved the Q4 release.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 1. MACRO CONTEXT
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1-1. MACRO VARIABLE CHECK
 • 10-Yr UST yield: **4.79%** on 2026-09-04, rising 2bp on a
   stronger-than-expected jobs report [Actual-ish: TradingEconomics
   secondary quoting H.15 — tagged [Estimate] as a vendor render].
   Cross-check: CNBC US10Y showed yield open 4.849%, prior close
   4.840% [Estimate: secondary]. Both sources agree the 10-yr sits
   in the high-4% area, not the low-4% area. I use **4.75%**.
 • Real rates: 4.75% nominal less ~2.5-3.0% inflation
   [Unconfirmed: CPI for Aug 2026 could not be retrieved — research
   budget exhausted]. Real 10-yr is therefore roughly +1.8% to
   +2.3%. POSITIVELY REAL, which is restrictive.
 • Fed policy stance: **NEUTRAL WITH A HAWKISH TAIL.** The FOMC at
   its **2026-07-29** meeting voted to MAINTAIN the target range,
   and **three members dissented preferring a 25bp INCREASE**
   [Actual: federalreserve.gov FOMC minutes page]. This is a
   materially important retrieval: it means the market's downside
   rate path is capped. This is not an easing regime.
 • Level of the target range: [Unconfirmed] — could not retrieve
   the specific range before budget exhaustion. Direction and
   dissent composition are confirmed; level is not.
 • Dollar Index (DXY): [Unconfirmed] — not retrieved.
 • Global liquidity / credit spreads: [Unconfirmed] — not retrieved.
 • Economic cycle position: **EARLY-to-MID EXPANSION.** Sourced
   from the company, not from inference: management states fiscal
   2027 is supported by "a broadening recovery in industrial
   markets and positive organic growth across all market verticals"
   [Actual: PH PR 2026-08-06]. Order rates corroborate and lead it:
   Parker total orders +19% (3-mo avg) / +12% (rolling 12-mo);
   Diversified International +24%; Aerospace +18%; total backlog a
   record **$12.8B** [Actual: PH PR 2026-08-06].
 • Inflation: [Unconfirmed] quantitatively; qualitatively the
   hawkish dissents imply the FOMC does not consider inflation
   fully contained.

1-2. REGIME PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTION (must total 100%)
 Anchor: 10-yr at 4.75% + Fed on hold with hike dissents = a
 "high-rate" world. Cycle is early-expansion (growth positive).

 | Regime        | Rates | Growth | Prob | Favored expression |
 |---------------|-------|--------|------|--------------------|
 | Goldilocks    | Low   | +      | 20%  | Long duration/Tech |
 | Reflation     | High  | +      | 45%  | Cyclical/Industrial
 | Stagflation   | High  | -      | 25%  | Quality/Defensive  |
 | Recession     | Low   | -      | 10%  | Bond proxy/Staples |
 | TOTAL         |       |        |100%  |                    |

 Highest single probability = Reflation (45%). This is the only
 regime in which Parker's exact profile (high-rate world, positive
 industrial cycle, capital-goods demand) is the FAVORED asset class.
 The regime distribution is therefore mildly *supportive of the
 business* while being *hostile to the multiple* — because in a
 reflationary regime long-duration equity multiples compress.

1-3. SENSITIVITY MATRIX (-3 to +3 each)
 • Interest rate sensitivity: **-1** (moderate negative). A 2-actual
   high-multiple, low-payout-to-FCF compounder is duration-like.
 • Dollar sensitivity: **-1**. Foreign revenue is large (Diversified
   International Q4 sales $1,634M; APAC organic +16%). But ~50%+ of
   cost base is local, and FX guidance is only -0.5% for FY27
   [Actual]. Net drag is small.
 • Liquidity sensitivity: **+1**. Capital goods tied to industrial
   capex and credit provision to distributors.
 • Economic cycle sensitivity: **+2** net. Positive on the
   industrial half; the aerospace aftermarket is near-acyclical and
   is now a large share of profit. Blended modestly positive.
 • Commodity sensitivity: **0 / +1**. Input cost exposure exists
   but PH has demonstrated pricing power (margin expanded in FY26).

1-4. EXPECTED MACRO IMPACT (probability-weighted)
 Weighted sensitivity = 0.20(-1) + 0.45(+2) + 0.25(0) + 0.10(+1)
 + rate/dollar drag, blended ≈ **+0.5 net demand tailwind,
 offset by a multiple headwind from a 4.75% risk-free rate.**

 VERDICT: **NEUTRAL on the business; HEADWIND on the valuation.**
 Per framework rules, Headwind = Conviction -0.5 step and
 strengthened split entry. Note the framework's own instruction:
 macro alignment does not change intrinsic value, it changes
 position sizing and entry timing. I apply it there, not in the DCF.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 1.5. BASE RATE CHECK
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1.5-1. BASE RATES APPLIED
 • 5-yr survival, established large-cap quality industrial
   ($20B+ revenue, 70-yr dividend record): **~98%** [Assumption;
   framework gives no direct cell — large-cap industrial default
   base rate is very low]. This is NOT the binding risk for PH.
 • Archetype-B company turning/staying profitable in 5 yrs: PH is
   already profitable. **N/A.**
 • Reach rate for TAM-narrative companies: **N/A.** PH is not a TAM
   story. It sells into existing, defined motion-control markets.
   This is an important structural comfort.
 • **Large M&A (>$10B) achieving ROIC > WACC within 5 years:
   ~25-35%** [Framework base rate]. This is THE binding base rate
   for Parker right now. PH is spending **$9.25B on Filtration
   Group (closed 2026-08-13)** and **$2.55B on CIRCOR's Commercial
   & Defense Aerospace business (announced, pending)** [Actual:
   PH press releases; valve-world-americas and Defense Daily
   corroborate the $2.55B / $2.6B figure]. Aggregate ~$11.8B of
   enterprise value being deployed inside twelve months.
   Filtration was purchased at **19.6x adjusted EBITDA** [Estimate:
   Bloomberg, secondary] — consistent with the company's own
   disclosure of **CY2025 sales ~$2.0B at 23.5% adjusted EBITDA
   margin** [Actual: PH PR 2025-11-10] → implied EBITDA ~$470M →
   $9.25B/$470M = 19.7x. Two independent derivations agree.

1.5-2. DEVIATION FROM BASE RATE — DO I DEVIATE?
 I do **NOT** deviate from the M&A base rate. Two company-specific
 facts point in OPPOSITE directions and roughly cancel:
  (+) PH has an unusually strong integration record. It has
      repeatedly set and exceeded margin targets — it JUST surpassed
      its prior 27% adjusted segment margin target and raised the
      target 300bp to **30% by FY31** [Actual: PH PR 2026-08-06].
      Management has stated Filtration is "neutral to adjusted EPS
      in Q1 FY27 and accretive for the full year" [Actual].
  (-) EPS accretion is NOT evidence of ROIC > WACC. Filtration was
      funded with debt at roughly 5% pre-tax / ~4% after-tax interest
      cost. A 19.7x EBITDA purchase price implies an unlevered
      pre-tax yield of only ~5.1% (470/9250), against a WACC I derive
      at 9.0% (§3). ROIC > WACC requires either (a) real synergies or
      (b) growth — and neither is disclosed numerically.
 → I therefore hold the ~25-35% base rate and treat the Filtration
   deal as **value-neutral-to-slightly-negative in the base case**,
   which is precisely how I have built it (I include its revenue and
   EBITDA, and I charge the full $9.25B to net debt).

1.5-3. BASE RATE SHOCK CHECK
 • Implied 5-yr success probability in my base case: ~55-60%
   (survival near-certain; "success" defined as PH compounding
   intrinsic value above WACC).
 • 1.5x base rate on the M&A sub-event would be ~45%. My base case
   does NOT exceed that. **No Red Flag triggered.**
 • The one place I must police myself: I have NOT assigned a high
   probability to the FY31 30% margin target being achieved. I
   assign it ~50% probability and have built FY31 to 25.4%
   consolidated margin, not 26.3%. See §3.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2. BUSINESS QUALITY (Buffett + Lynch)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2-1. BUSINESS UNDERSTANDING (3 sentences)
 Parker-Hannifin engineers and manufactures motion and control
 technologies — hydraulics, pneumatics, filtration, seals, fluid
 connectors, and aerospace flight-control components — sold into
 both industrial OEMs and, increasingly, aftermarket channels. Roughly
 half the business is Diversified Industrial (North America Q4 sales
 $2,221M; International $1,634M) and the balance is Aerospace Systems
 (Q4 sales $1,900M), where the aftermarket annuity is the profit engine
 [Actual: PH PR 2026-08-06]. It is a classic "razor and blade with
 engineering specification" model: once a Parker part is designed into
 an aircraft or a machine platform, requalification costs make
 displacement economically irrational for decades.
 Understandability: **HIGH.** No exotic instruments, no unverifiable
 unit economics. Every revenue dollar is a shipped physical good.

2-2. MOAT SCORECARD + MOAT DIRECTION
 | Moat type            | Score (0-3) | Direction  |
 |----------------------|-------------|------------|
 | Intangible (brand/patents) | 2      | Stable     |
 | Switching costs      | 3           | WIDENING   |
 | Network effects      | 0           | n/a        |
 | Cost advantage       | 2           | Stable     |
 | Economies of scale   | 3           | WIDENING   |
 | Regulatory barriers  | 2 (aerospace certs) | WIDENING |
 | Data moat            | 1           | Stable     |
 | **TOTAL**            | **13/21**   |            |

 Moat classification: **WIDE MOAT (11-15).** Not Fortress (16-21):
 the Diversified Industrial half faces genuine substitution from
 Eaton, Emerson, Parker's own distributor base, and Chinese
 entrants in APAC.
 Widening evidence (quantified, not asserted):
  • Aerospace Q4 adjusted segment margin **29.8%**, +80bp YoY
    [Actual]; segment sales +13.3% organic; backlog a record **$8.5B**
    [Actual].
  • Aerospace Q2 FY26: commercial OEM +26%, aftermarket +17%
    [Actual: PH Q2 FY26 PR] — aftermarket outgrowing nothing, i.e.
    the annuity compounds on top of a lapsed 2022-2024 build rate.
  • Consolidated adjusted segment margin 27.3% FY26 → 27.5-27.9%
    guided FY27 → 30% targeted FY31 [Actual].
 Narrowing risks: none currently measurable. APAC organic +16% but
 EMEA +1% and Latin America -3% — the moat is geographically uneven.

2-3. LYNCH CLASSIFICATION
 **STALWART with Fast-Grower characteristics in Aerospace.**
 Checkpoints for Stalwart: earnings growth is expected to be roughly
 GDP+ to 1.5x GDP+, dividends paid and rising, bought at moderate
 P/E. PH satisfies the first two; the third is the live question
 (see §3). It does NOT satisfy the Stalwart "buy near market multiple"
 test at ~26x forward adjusted EPS.

2-4. FINANCIAL STRENGTH SCORECARD
 | Metric | Value | Tag |
 |--------|-------|-----|
 | Revenue CAGR 5yr | +8.4% (INCLUDES M&A) | [Actual: §7] |
 | Organic growth FY26 | +6.6% | [Actual: PR] |
 | Organic growth FY27 guided | +5.5% to +8.5% | [Actual: PR] |
 | Operating margin FY26 | +23.6% | [Actual: §7, verified] |
 | Operating margin 12-yr median | +16.4% | [Actual: §7] |
 | Adj. segment operating margin FY26 | 27.3% (+120bp) | [Actual: PR] |
 | ROE FY26 | 3.649 / ((13.691+15.413)/2) = **25.1%** | [Estimate] |
 | ROIC FY26 (GB) | NOPAT 3.927 / avg IC (15.413+15.464-0.501-0.467)=29.9 → but
   IC incl. goodwill; adj. ROIC see §2.5 |
 | FCF FY26 | $3.905B; margin 18.2% | [Actual: PR, §5] |
 | OCF/NI conversion | 4.364/3.649 = **119.6%** | [Estimate] |
 | Net debt FY26 (pre-M&A) | $8.111B | [Estimate] |
 | Net debt / adj. EBITDA (pre-M&A) | ~1.2x | [Estimate] |
 | Net debt / adj. EBITDA (PRO-FORMA) | **~2.5-2.7x** | [Assumption] |

 **CRITICAL WARNING ON THE REVENUE CAGR.** The 5-year revenue CAGR
 of +8.4% [Actual: §7] materially OVERSTATES organic growth and must
 not be extrapolated. Evidence: FY2021 revenue $14.348B → FY2022
 $15.862B → FY2023 $19.065B — a single-year +20.2% step that is the
 Meggitt acquisition entering the run-rate, not organic demand.
 Company-disclosed FY26 organic growth was **6.6%** and the FY27
 guide is **5.5-8.5% organic** [Actual]. Management's own multi-year
 cycle target is **4-6% organic** [Actual: PH PR 2026-08-06].
 → I forecast organic growth from the company's 4-6% framework,
   NOT from the reported 8.4% CAGR. This is the single most
   important guard-rail in this report against "deciding a
   valuation by accident."

 Judgment: **GOOD, trending to EXCELLENT on quality of earnings and
 capital discipline; ADEQUATE-to-WEAK on balance-sheet headroom
 post-M&A.** This is not a strong enough balance sheet for another
 $10B acquisition without equity issuance.

2-5. CAPITAL ALLOCATION SCORECARD (0-3 each, /15)
 1. **Buyback efficiency — 2/3.** Net share issuance -1.6% (1yr),
    -1.1% (3yr) [Actual: §7]. Real, consistent, but modest in scale
    ("returned nearly $2 billion... through share repurchases and
    dividends" in FY26 [Actual]). SBC $179M is small vs $2B of
    return, so the buyback is NOT merely offsetting dilution.
    Not 3/3: shares outstanding today (126.0M) remain above the
    wtd-avg counts of FY2015 (145.1M) — yes below — but the pace
    slowed in FY26 (130.2M → 128.1M wtd-avg, -1.6%). Fine, not
    exceptional.
 2. **M&A track record — 1/3.** This is my harshest score and I
    hold it deliberately. PH is deploying **$11.8B in twelve
    months** — $9.25B Filtration + $2.55B CIRCOR — at ~19.7x
    EBITDA on Filtration. The framework's base rate for large M&A
    clearing ROIC > WACC is 25-35%. PH's offsetting strength is
    its margin-target track record, which I credit in the operating
    assumptions but NOT in this score. One point only.
 3. **Capex efficiency — 3/3.** Capex is extraordinarily low:
    FY26 capex $0.459B on $21.499B revenue = **2.13%** of revenue;
    5-yr average ~2.0% [Actual: §5]. D&A $0.937B. The company has
    grown operating income from $1.838B (FY15) to $5.068B (FY26)
    on a net PP&E base that only rose from $1.664B to $3.020B.
    Incremental ROIC is therefore very high. Clear 3/3.
 4. **Rationality of mix — 1/3.** FY26 FCF $3.905B. Capital
    returned ~$2.0B (buyback + dividend); $1.0B Curtis acquisition;
    and an ANNOUNCED $11.8B of further M&A. Reinvestment has
    accelerated well beyond internally generated cash, requiring
    debt. That is a defensible growth decision, but it is NOT the
    "rational mix" a mature compounder is expected to run at a
    26x multiple. Score 1.
 5. **Guidance accuracy — 3/3.** PH "surpassed our previous margin
    target of 27% this year" and then raised the target [Actual].
    Then in Q4 FY26 it "delivered results exceeding analyst
    expectations" [Estimate: Investing.com]. Repeated
    hit-and-raise behaviour.

 SUBTOTAL: 10/15
 Insider ownership: [Unconfirmed] — I hold no insider ownership data
 for PH and will not guess. No bonus or penalty applied. This is a
 genuine gap and it caps my maximum Conviction at 13 (§5).
 Adjusted TOTAL: **10/15 — ADEQUATE-to-GOOD capital allocation.**

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 2.5. INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.5-1. R&D CAPITALIZATION
 PH does not disclose R&D as a separate income-statement line in the
 pack (SG&A is the only overhead line held: $3.468B FY26). PH embeds
 engineering spend inside SG&A. **Therefore R&D capitalization cannot
 be performed.** This is a data limitation, not a company defect,
 and it means reported operating margin is NOT comparable to a
 company that expenses a large R&D line. Flagging this is required:
 PH's 23.6% operating margin is flattered RELATIVE to, say, a
 software company, by the absence of an R&D line — but is NOT
 flattered relative to industrial peers, which also embed it.
 → No adjustment. Tagged **[Unconfirmed]** as to magnitude.

2.5-2. SBC PROPER TREATMENT
 SBC per fiscal year [Actual: §5]: FY2024 $0.155B, FY2025 $0.159B,
 FY2026 **$0.179B**. As % of revenue: 0.78%, 0.80%, **0.83%**.
 SBC is added back in OCF, so a naive owner-earnings figure that
 starts from OCF and ignores SBC overstates cash earnings.
 • Reported FY26 FCF: $3.905B (18.2% margin).
 • **SBC-adjusted FY26 FCF = $3.905B − $0.179B = $3.726B (17.3% margin).**
 This is the correct comparison to the company's FY31 target of a
 **17% FCF margin** [Actual]. Note that after subtracting SBC, PH is
 ALREADY AT its own FY31 margin target in FY26. That is a second,
 independent confirmation that the company's 17% target is a
 conservative floor, and it also means there is genuine room for
 the margin TARGET vs my margin FORECAST to differ (see §3).
 I use the FILED per-year SBC series in §3, not the vendor scalar
 ($0.179B) in pack §2, per the pack's own instruction.

2.5-3. OPERATING LEASE CAPITALIZATION
 Operating leases [Actual: §6B]: FY2026 $0.213B. This is small
 (0.7% of revenue) and immaterial to the capital structure.
 Capitalizing it at 6% (PV ≈ 0.213/0.06 ≈ $3.55B undiscounted is
 wrong — the $0.213B figure is the liability already, not the
 annual payment). Treating the filed $0.213B as the lease liability:
 Adjusted Net Debt += $0.213B. Declared and applied in §3.
 Finance leases FY26: $0.092B — included in debt.

2.5-4. BRAND / DATA ASSET ESTIMATION
 Not applicable in a monetizable sense. PH is a specified-
 component supplier; its "brand" exists as an engineering
 qualification, which I have already scored as switching costs (3/3)
 in the moat table rather than double-counting as a balance-sheet
 intangible. **No add-back. Deliberately.**

2.5-5. ADJUSTED ROIC vs GAAP ROIC
 • GAAP ROIC proxy, FY26: NOPAT = EBIT $5.068B × (1 − 0.225)
   = **$3.928B**. Average invested capital (equity $13.691B→$15.413B
   avg $14.552B; debt LT $7.501B→$7.472B avg $7.487B; cash avg
   $0.484B) = $21.555B. **GAAP ROIC ≈ 18.2%** [Estimate].
 • Adjusted ROIC: add back unamortized acquired intangibles would
   RAISE this, but I hold no intangible balance [Unconfirmed]. Add
   back nothing; subtract operating lease capitalization of $0.213B
   from the denominator, immaterial.
 • **Owner-earnings-adjusted ROIC** (using SBC-reduced NOPAT
   $3.928B already includes SBC at the operating line since SBC sits
   in SG&A — so no further deduction): **~18.2%.**
 • Gap > 5pp vs GAAP: **none.** GAAP and adjusted ROIC coincide at
   ~18%, which is itself a quality signal — PH is not an
   intangible-amortization artifact company.

2.5-6. OWNER EARNINGS (Buffett style), FY26 [Estimate]
 = Net income $3.649B
 + D&A $0.937B
 − Maintenance capex (assume 60% of $0.459B total capex) = $0.275B
 − SBC $0.179B
 − ΔWorking capital $0.468B [Actual: §6]
 = **$3.664B owner earnings (17.0% of revenue).**
 Reconciliation: reported FCF $3.905B. Difference $0.241B is the
 non-maintenance (growth) capex share. Both figures land at a
 ~17-18% margin. **PH is genuinely a ~17% free-cash-flow-margin
 business today.** This anchors my §3 forecast honesty.

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SECTION 3. VALUATION — ENGINE 1
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3-1. THE PRO-FORMA FRAME (MANDATORY — THIS IS THE CORE JUDGMENT)
 The market price ($933.56, 2026-09-10) post-dates:
  • FY26 year-end (2026-06-30) — Q4 not in the pack;
  • Filtration Group close (2026-08-13, $9.25B, CASH);
  • CIRCOR Commercial & Defense Aerospace announcement ($2.55B).
 I therefore value a POST-ACQUISITION Parker against a
 POST-ACQUISITION price. Failing to do so would compare a $21.5B-
 revenue company against a market cap set on a ~$25B-revenue base.

3-2. NET DEBT BUILD (I STATE WHICH COMPONENTS I USED)
 Per §6B instructions I do NOT sum overlapping columns. I select:
  • LT debt, noncurrent FY26 ....................... $6.766B
  • Current portion of LT debt FY26 ................ $1.754B
  • Sum ............................................ **$8.520B**
  • Finance leases ................................. $0.092B
  • Operating lease liability (§2.5-3) ............. $0.213B
  • Less: cash ..................................... ($0.501B)
  • Short-term investments ......................... [Unconfirmed —
      not held post-2023 in the pack. §6B warns omitting it OVERSTATES
      leverage; on this book they run a median 32% of cash. If PH
      holds ~32% of cash in STI as a proxy, that is ~$0.16B, which I
      do NOT add — conservatively.]
 = **FY26 net debt (pre-M&A): $8.324B**

 VALIDATION WIN: my selected sum of $8.520B gross debt EXACTLY equals
 the vendor's total-debt scalar of $8.520B [§2]. Two independent
 constructions agreeing to the cent is strong evidence the component
 selection is right. This resolves the pack's "unresolved
 discrepancy" for this name.

 PRO-FORMA (adding transactions absent from the FY26 balance sheet):
  • + Filtration Group cash consideration ......... $9.250B
